result.markdown:
Yes. Based on the current information I found, there are several good options in **Newcastle, NSW**, but I’d distinguish between firms that do TPD as part of a broad personal-injury practice and firms that are genuinely focused on **superannuation/insurance claims**.

### My Newcastle shortlist

| Firm | Why I’d consider them | Best fit |
|---|---|---|
| **Law Partners Injury Lawyers Newcastle** | Has a dedicated TPD/superannuation practice and a Newcastle office at 400 Hunter St. [lawpartners.com.au](https://lawpartners.com.au/superannuation-tpd-lawyers?utm_source=chatgpt.com) | **Strong all-round local option** |
| **Burke Mead Lawyers** | Newcastle-based; led by Emma Mead, a Law Society of NSW **Accredited Specialist in Personal Injury Law**. They specifically handle TPD, superannuation and insurance claims. [www.burkemeadlawyers.com.au](https://www.burkemeadlawyers.com.au/superannuation-and-insurance/?utm_source=chatgpt.com) | **Excellent local specialist/personal-injury option** |
| **Turner Freeman Lawyers** | Newcastle lawyer Jessica Thomas has 10+ years in personal injury and specifically lists superannuation, TPD and insurance claims. [www.turnerfreeman.com.au](https://www.turnerfreeman.com.au/team/jessica-thomas/?utm_source=chatgpt.com) | **Good if you want an experienced individual lawyer** |
| **GMP Superannuation Lawyers** | The Newcastle business listing identifies it specifically as an insurance attorney, which makes it particularly relevant to super/insurance rather than general compensation. | **Worth investigating for a specialist super/insurance approach** |
| **Berrill & Watson** | Not Newcastle-office based, but they explicitly handle TPD, income protection and superannuation claims for Newcastle and regional NSW. Their principals have spent their careers specialising in super/insurance. [www.berrillwatson.com.au](https://www.berrillwatson.com.au/about/tpd-nsw/?utm_source=chatgpt.com) | **My pick if specialist TPD/super expertise matters more than having a Newcastle office** |
| **The Law Office of Conrad Curry** | Specifically advertises Newcastle TPD, superannuation and income-protection claims, including insurer negotiations, AFCA disputes and court proceedings. [conradcurrylaw.com.au](https://conradcurrylaw.com.au/tpd-lawyers-newcastle/?utm_source=chatgpt.com) | **Good for a disputed/complex claim** |


### 🥇 Who I'd call first

**1. Berrill & Watson — if the claim is primarily TPD/super/insurance**

This is probably the firm I'd put at the top of the list **on specialist expertise alone**. They say their practice is centred on superannuation and insurance disputes, including TPD and income protection, rather than treating TPD as one service among many. Tom Cobban, one of their principals, has worked his entire career in superannuation and insurance claims. [www.berrillwatson.com.au](https://www.berrillwatson.com.au/about/tpd-nsw/?utm_source=chatgpt.com)

They also have recent client feedback specifically concerning TPD and superannuation claims, including a 2026 review describing specialist advice throughout a TPD claim. [www.berrillwatson.com.au](https://www.berrillwatson.com.au/about/what-our-clients-say/?utm_source=chatgpt.com)

**2. Burke Mead — if you want a strong Newcastle-based firm**

I'd put **Burke Mead** very high if you'd prefer a genuinely local Newcastle practice. Their Newcastle office is on Bolton Street, and they specifically handle superannuation and insurance claims. Emma Mead is a Law Society of NSW Accredited Specialist in Personal Injury Law. [www.burkemeadlawyers.com.au](https://www.burkemeadlawyers.com.au/superannuation-and-insurance/?utm_source=chatgpt.com)

An additional advantage is that they say they **act only for injured people, never insurers**, which is useful when you're dealing with an insurance company or super fund. [www.burkemeadlawyers.com.au](https://www.burkemeadlawyers.com.au/team/?utm_source=chatgpt.com)

**3. Law Partners — strong established Newcastle option**

They have a dedicated TPD/superannuation practice and a Newcastle office at **400 Hunter Street**. [lawpartners.com.au](https://lawpartners.com.au/superannuation-tpd-lawyers?utm_source=chatgpt.com) This would be another firm I'd include when obtaining competing initial assessments.

### One important distinction

If your situation is **“I haven't lodged the TPD claim yet”**, I'd look for someone experienced in preparing the medical evidence and interpreting the particular fund's TPD definition.

If it's **“my TPD claim has been rejected/delayed”**, I'd place more weight on a lawyer who regularly handles **insurer disputes, internal reviews and AFCA proceedings**. Conrad Curry, for example, expressly advertises assistance with rejected/disputed claims through internal review and AFCA, as well as court proceedings. [conradcurrylaw.com.au](https://conradcurrylaw.com.au/tpd-lawyers-newcastle/?utm_source=chatgpt.com)

And if you have **both TPD and income-protection/salary-continuance insurance**, Berrill & Watson becomes particularly interesting because those are core areas of their practice. [www.berrillwatson.com.au](https://www.berrillwatson.com.au/about/tpd-nsw/?utm_source=chatgpt.com)

### My practical recommendation

I'd get **2–3 initial assessments before signing anything**:

1. **Berrill & Watson** — specialist super/insurance benchmark.
2. **Burke Mead** — strong Newcastle-based comparison.
3. **Law Partners** or **Conrad Curry** — another established option.

Ask each one:
- Have you handled **my particular super fund/insurer** before?
- How many **TPD claims** does the lawyer personally handle?
- Do you handle **declined claims and AFCA**, or only straightforward applications?
- What percentage of the settlement/benefit could go toward **legal fees and costs**?
- Is it genuinely **no-win-no-fee**, and are there any disbursements or deductions if the claim succeeds?
- Do you investigate **all of my super funds**, in case I have multiple TPD policies?

If you tell me **(a) whether your TPD claim has already been rejected, (b) the super fund/insurer, and (c) whether you're also claiming income protection**, I can narrow this to the **best 2–3 lawyers for your particular situation** and compare their fees, reviews, experience and contact details.

An additional advantage is that they say they **act only for injured people, never insurers**, which is useful when you're dealing with an insurance company or super fund. [www.burkemeadlawyers.com.au](https://www.burkemeadlawyers.com.au/team/?utm_source=chatgpt.com)

**3. Law Partners — strong established Newcastle option**

They have a dedicated TPD/superannuation practice and a Newcastle office at **400 Hunter Street**. [lawpartners.com.au](https://lawpartners.com.au/superannuation-tpd-lawyers?utm_source=chatgpt.com) This would be another firm I'd include when obtaining competing initial assessments.

### One important distinction

If your situation is **“I haven't lodged the TPD claim yet”**, I'd look for someone experienced in preparing the medical evidence and interpreting the particular fund's TPD definition.

If it's **“my TPD claim has been rejected/delayed”**, I'd place more weight on a lawyer who regularly handles **insurer disputes, internal reviews and AFCA proceedings**. Conrad Curry, for example, expressly advertises assistance with rejected/disputed claims through internal review and AFCA, as well as court proceedings. [conradcurrylaw.com.au](https://conradcurrylaw.com.au/tpd-lawyers-newcastle/?utm_source=chatgpt.com)

And if you have **both TPD and income-protection/salary-continuance insurance**, Berrill & Watson becomes particularly interesting because those are core areas of their practice. [www.berrillwatson.com.au](https://www.berrillwatson.com.au/about/tpd-nsw/?utm_source=chatgpt.com)

### My practical recommendation

I'd get **2–3 initial assessments before signing anything**:

1. **Berrill & Watson** — specialist super/insurance benchmark.
2. **Burke Mead** — strong Newcastle-based comparison.
3. **Law Partners** or **Conrad Curry** — another established option.

Ask each one:
- Have you handled **my particular super fund/insurer** before?
- How many **TPD claims** does the lawyer personally handle?
- Do you handle **declined claims and AFCA**, or only straightforward applications?
- What percentage of the settlement/benefit could go toward **legal fees and costs**?
- Is it genuinely **no-win-no-fee**, and are there any disbursements or deductions if the claim succeeds?
- Do you investigate **all of my super funds**, in case I have multiple TPD policies?

If you tell me **(a) whether your TPD claim has already been rejected, (b) the super fund/insurer, and (c) whether you're also claiming income protection**, I can narrow this to the **best 2–3 lawyers for your particular situation** and compare their fees, reviews, experience and contact details.
